Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Inc. Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, press star then one on your telephone keypad. There may be a brief wait time prior to the introduction of your question. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge Inc.'s Third Quarter Fiscal 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Jordan Lee, CTO; Taylor Brooks, Chief Revenue Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Product Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Marketing Officer; and Lisa Moreno, Chief Customer Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge Inc.'s performance for the third quarter of fiscal 2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our CloudForge Copilot and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on eight key areas: raising our full-year revenue guidance, delivering strong NRR performance, expanding gross margins, optimizing our cost of revenue breakdown, controlling operating expenses, shifting our customer mix favorably, advancing our capital allocation strategy, and enhancing sales efficiency.

These accomplishments highlight our disciplined approach to growth in a competitive SaaS environment, positioning us for sustained momentum. We are confident in our ability to continue this trajectory and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $118 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin was 82.5%, and operating income was $18 million.

Let me provide more color on these results and our outlook. First, on gross margins, which continue to reflect the scalability of our SaaS model. For Q3 fiscal 2024, we delivered a GAAP gross margin of 82.5%, up 130 basis points year-over-year from 81.2% in the prior year and 70 basis points sequentially from 81.8% in Q2. Non-GAAP gross margin expanded to 84.1%, a 160 basis point improvement year-over-year, excluding about $2.4 million in stock-based compensation and amortization from our recent WorkflowAI acquisition.

This expansion stems from several factors. Economies of scale in our infrastructure were the biggest driver, contributing around 80 basis points year-over-year. With ARR growing 28% to $428 million, we improved data center utilization to 78% from 72%, using our ForgeOptics AI for predictive planning across AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. This allowed volume discounts on reserved instances, cutting costs per TB by 25% compared to spot pricing last year. Hosting and bandwidth, 65% of cost of revenue, fell 4.2 points as a percentage of revenue, even with a 15% rise in GPU costs for Copilot features—we offset that with 30% lower inference latency through model optimizations.

Product mix shifts added 50 basis points, as enterprise customers, now 62% of dollar-based net retention, bring higher margins via usage-based pricing and premium add-ons like ForgeSecure. Wins like a major bank's 150,000-seat expansion helped. Regionally, Americas margins were 83.2%, EMEA jumped to 85.7% with GDPR tiers and OVHcloud partnerships, and APAC was 79.4% due to localization but set to improve. Sequentially, technical moves like migrating to ForgeDB cut query costs 22%, and our MarginForge program reduced onboarding costs 18%.

Looking ahead, we see Q4 GAAP margins at 83-84%, expanding further as ARR nears $500 million.

Turning to our cost of revenue breakdown, which totaled around $21 million this quarter, or 18% of revenue, driving our strong margins. Hosting and infrastructure was the largest at about 45% of COR, or 15% of revenue, covering compute, storage, and bandwidth on our multi-cloud setup. It was flat sequentially but down 8% year-over-year as a percentage, thanks to Graviton instances and Spot VMs saving 30-40% on AI workloads, plus CDN deals with Cloudflare reducing egress 15%. We're pushing serverless and FinOps tools for more savings.

Customer support and success was 30% of COR, stable at 10% of revenue despite 28% ARR growth, with AI chatbots resolving 45% of L1 tickets and predictive tools boosting retention. Professional services at 15% declined 5% quarter-over-quarter as PLG takes hold—60% self-onboarding now—and utilization hit 75%. Other costs like royalties and payments were 10%, up slightly with new features.

Overall, COR declined 150 basis points year-over-year, targeting sub-32% by FY2025 through AI automation and PLG.

On NRR, a cornerstone of our flywheel, we hit 118% in Q3—our 11th straight quarter above 115%, up 300 basis points sequentially and outpacing peers like Snowflake and Datadog. From a $450 million ARR cohort base, expansion added 27 points via module upsells (68% of top 500 customers), cross-sells into Workflow Automation at 42% attach, and data lakehouse growth. Contraction was -4 points, bettered by health scores and 22% pricing realization. Churn was -3 points at 2.8% gross dollar, with logo churn 1.2% in low-ACV.

Broad-based: North America 122%, EMEA 120%, APAC 108%. AI initiatives like ForgeAI yield 2.5x expansion; we expect 117-119% in Q4.

Operating expenses show discipline: Total non-GAAP opex was about $85 million, up 18% year-over-year but down 300 basis points to 72% of revenue. R&D at $32 million or 21%, flat sequentially, with 40% to AI like natural language querying, headcount up in Bangalore/Tel Aviv for security. S&M at $50 million or 33%, down 450 basis points, CAC payback 16 months, inbound leads up 30%. G&A $36 million or 24%, leveraging remote work and tech upgrades. We're on track for Rule of 40 at 55%.

Customer mix shifted favorably: Enterprise (>100k ACV) now 48% of customers but 78% of ARR, up from 72%, with 38% YoY growth versus 16% SMB. Enterprise NRR 142%, wins like $15M Fortune 50. Regions: NA 72%, EMEA 52% growth. Tilting to enterprise for margins (86% vs 81%), Land-and-Expand 2.0 with 65% pilots converting.

Sales efficiency improved: Cycles compressed to 112 days, top quartile, via PLG (28% new ARR), enablement tools. Conversions: MQL-SQO 32%, SQO-close 38%, overall 12.5%. NA 105 days, pipeline 4.2x target.

Capital allocation prioritizes organic reinvestment (65-70% FCF), like $580M R&D for Zenith Forge LLM—wait, our ForgeAI—boosting NRR. Capex 4-5% for cloud. M&A 20-25%, like $425M DataPulse for 15% cybersecurity ARR. Shareholder returns: $280M buybacks. Balance sheet: $180 million cash, no debt.

We continue investing in R&D for innovation. Cash position strong at $180 million.

Wrapping with full-year guidance: Raising FY2024 revenue to $475 million to $485 million, 26-28% growth from $376 million FY2023, ahead of prior $450-460 million. YTD $348 million implies Q4 $127-137 million, 30% sequential. ARR $482 million, +31%. Subscription $440-450 million, +29-31%; services flat $35 million. New ARR $42 million Q3, large deals 45%. NRR 116%, Copilot 28% ARR. Americas 72%, EMEA 18% +38%, APAC 10% +45%. RPO $620 million +42%, pipeline 3.2x Q4.

This embeds AI tailwinds, enterprise thaw. Risks: federal delays, competition. But leverage and cash support aggression.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee for a technology update.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, including zero-trust enhancements and multi-cloud orchestration.

And now Emily Vargas will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Emily Vargas:
Thank you, Jordan. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the launch of our new AI-driven Predictive Analytics Engine. This new feature significantly improves real-time insights and workflow automation. We are seeing strong adoption of this feature, which aligns with our product strategy of embedding agentic AI across the stack.

Raj Singh:
Thank you, Emily. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 30% increase in website traffic and a 25% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, particularly ABM in enterprise verticals.

Lisa Moreno:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to delivering exceptional customer experiences and this quarter, we focused on improving our customer support and onboarding processes. As a result, we have seen a 15% increase in customer satisfaction scores, driven by AI chatbots and success pods.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. To ask a question, press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of CloudForge Copilot on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, what's the competitive landscape like, and how do you plan to differentiate yourselves?

Taylor Brooks:
Thanks, Ben. CloudForge Copilot has been transformative for our growth, contributing 28% of total ARR now, up from 18% a year ago, and driving over $42 million in new ARR this quarter through multi-year upsells. Attach rates are strong at 68% among eligible customers, exceeding our initial expectations by 20% due to seamless integrations with CRM tools like Salesforce. The competitive landscape includes players like Salesforce Einstein and ServiceNow Vancouver, but we're differentiating with fine-tuned LLMs on customer data for predictive workflows, proprietary ForgeAI models, and superior low-code extensibility—yielding 2.5x higher expansion rates and positioning us in the $100B workflow automation market.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Priya Patel with Morgan Stanley.

Priya Patel:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, what are your expected ROI from these investments, and what are the key challenges you anticipate?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Priya. International expansion is a priority, with APAC as a high-growth focus—currently 10% of revenue but accelerating to 45% growth. Key targets are Japan and Australia, leveraging hyperscaler partnerships like AWS and Azure for data sovereignty. We expect ROI of 3x within 18 months through localized AI and Tokyo data center. Challenges include FX headwinds, longer cycles, and regulations, but our GDPR-aligned features and regional teams are mitigating them effectively.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan.

David Kim:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what are your strategies to improve customer retention, what's the impact of pricing changes on churn, and what are your long-term targets for NRR?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. Churn management is proactive amid macro pressures—we're at 2.8% gross dollar churn, below 4% target. NRR trended to 118% this quarter, steady above 115%. Strategies include ML health scores, AI onboarding, and pods boosting NPS to 72. Pricing adjustments of 5-7% on renewals had no material impact, actually aiding retention with 22% realization. Long-term NRR target is 110%+, with upside to 120% from cohort aging and AI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Barclays.

Laura Chen:
Can you provide more color on customer acquisition costs (CAC) and payback periods for new customers?

Mike Patel:
Sure, Laura. CAC is trending efficiently at around $250K for enterprise, with payback now 16 months, improved from 19 months year-over-year, thanks to inbound leads up 30% and PLG conversions. Overall LTV/CAC is 4.2x, supporting Rule of 40.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
